etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English flour, from Anglo-Norman flur, from Latin flōrem, accusative of flōs, from Proto-Italic *flōs, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleh₃- (“to thrive, bloom”). Doublet of flour.

Partly displaced native Old English blostma, whence Modern English blossom.

definitions.definition: A colorful, conspicuous structure associated with angiosperms, frequently scented and attracting various insects, and which may or may not be used for sexual reproduction.

quote.citation: 1653, William Basse, “Clio, or The First Muse; in 9 Eglogues in Honor of 9 Vertues. As It was in His Dayes Intended. [Munday. Laurinella. Eglogue. Of True and Chast Love.]”, in J[ohn] P[ayne] C[ollier], editor, The Pastorals and Other Workes of William Basse. […] (Miscellaneous Tracts, Temp. Eliz. & Jac. I), [London: s.n.], published 1870, →OCLC:
quote.text: O Laurinella! little doſt thou wot / How fraile a flower thou doſt ſo highly prize: / Beauty's the flower, but love the flower-pot / That muſt preſerve it, els it quickly dyes.

quote.citation: 1954 July 29, J[ohn] R[onald] R[euel] Tolkien, “A Long-Expected Party”, in The Fellowship of the Ring: Being the First Part of The Lord of the Rings, New York, N.Y.: Ballantine Books, published September 1973, →ISBN:
quote.text: The flowers glowed red and golden: snapdragons and sunflowers, and nasturtians trailing all over the turf walls and peeping in at the round windows.

definitions.definition: (botany) A reproductive structure in angiosperms (flowering plants), often conspicuously colourful and typically including sepals, petals, and either or both stamens and/or a pistil.

quote.citation: 1894, H. G. Wells, The Flowering of the Strange Orchid:
quote.text: You know, Darwin studied their fertilisation, and showed that the whole structure of an ordinary orchid flower was contrived in order that moths might carry the pollen from plant to plant.

definitions.definition: A plant that bears flowers, especially a plant that is small and lacks wood.
The stem of a flowering plant with the blossom or blossoms attached, used for decoration, as a gift, etc.
(uncountable, usually with in) Of plants, a state of bearing blooms.
(euphemistic, hypocoristic) The vulva, especially the labia majora.

quote.citation: 1749, [John Cleland], “(Please specify the letter or volume)”, in Memoirs of a Woman of Pleasure [Fanny Hill], London:  […]  [Thomas Parker] for G. Fenton [i.e., Fenton and Ralph Griffiths] […], →OCLC, page 106:
quote.text: [F]or ſtill, that my virgin-flower was yet uncrop'd never once enter'd into his head, and he would have thought it idling with time and words to have queſtion'd me upon it.

quote.citation: 1893, Emily Gerard, The Voice of a Flower, page 44:
quote.text: So was it asserted, that whenever a maiden was destined to die unmarried, as surely would the plant wither away and perish, and if a dughter of the Renseccos lost her honour or had given away her flower to an unworthy lover, then would the flower be blighted overnight.

quote.citation: 2018, Satu Lidman, Gender, Violence and Attitudes: Lessons from Early Modern Europe:
quote.text: In some local tradditions a fallen bride was married wearing a crown of straw rather than a garland of flowers, to symbolize her loss of  virginity – the wilting of her flower.

quote.citation: 2019, Shaun Barger, Mage Against the Machine, page 146:
quote.text: "Our flesh as one!" he laughed, speaking loudly. "Sweating bodies entwined in carnal passion! As I plunge myself deep into her lady flower, again and again and again— !"

definitions.definition: The best examples or representatives of a group.

quote.text: At Floddon hyllys, / Our bowys, our byllys / Slew all the floure / Of theyr honoure.

quote.text: the flower of the chivalry of all Spain

quote.citation: 1915, Katharine Tynan, The Golden Boy:
quote.text: In times of peace, so clean and bright, / And with a new-washed morning face, / He walked Pall Mall, a goodly sight, / The finished flower of all the race.

definitions.definition: The best state of things; the prime.

quote.citation: 1842, Alfred Tennyson, “Lady Clara Vere de Vere”, in Poems. […], volume I, London: Edward Moxon, […], →OCLC, stanza 2, page 156:

quote.text: NO lady fair in hall or bower, / In days when knighthood was in flower, / Or high-born dame with jewels set, / Or Tudor or Plantagenet, / E’er wore enwreath’d on form and face / Thy royal robe of richest grace.

quote.text: Exposed to a moderate fire in subliming pots, [brimstone] rises all into dry, and almost tasteless, flowers; whereas being exposed to a naked fire, it affords store of a saline and fretting liquor.

definitions.definition: A figure of speech; an ornament of style.
(printing) Ornamental type used chiefly for borders around pages, cards, etc.

quote.citation: 1841, William Savage, A Dictionary of the Art of Printing:
quote.text: I pointed out to the late Mr. Catherwood, of the firm of Caslon and Catherwood, the inconvenience of both these modes of cutting flowers,

definitions.definition: A delicate, fragile, or oversensitive person.

quote.text: […]  she whispered leaning over and kissing her forehead; and then added, 'Mummy loves you, precious flower.'

quote.citation: 2016, Barbara Ann Wright, Paladins of the Storm Lord:
quote.text: “Take care of yourself out there, Brown, you delicate flower.”

quote.citation: 2021, Alica McKenna-Johnson, The Unicorn's Scion:
quote.text: “Come on, you delicate flower, we just need to nap. It will be fine.”

definitions.definition: (figurative, chiefly in the plural) Credit, recognition.

quote.citation: 2010, M. Joyce Dickerson, A Tribute to 101 Incredible Women of Distinction Who Influenced My Life From My House to the White House:
quote.text: It has been my desire to find a way to express my gratitude to these women for quite some time but I really did not know how to give them their flowers as a method to tell them thanks.

quote.citation: 2011, Tommy Hicks, Game of My Life Alabama Crimson Tide, page 149:
quote.text: I was able to give Coach Bryant his flowers while he was alive, and I have always been thankful I was able to do that.

quote.citation: 2023, Torry Smith, Alpha's Unexpected Luna:
quote.text: Gonzalo managed to fake a smile. When will anyone ever give him his flowers? His hard work kept him and his kingdom this far. Wasn't anyone going to acknowledge the fact?

quote.text: Sabrina Carpenter is, finally, getting her flowers. Ever since demurely (I don't use that word lightly!!!) performing what would become the song of 2024 as part of her Coachella set—no, literally, "Espresso" just won the MTV Video Music Award for Song of the Year—all eyes have been on 'Brina.

definitions.definition: (uncountable, slang) Cannabis.
